issues.description: The 'adj-free-list' adjunction is mathematically incorrect as defined. For an adjunction F ⊣ G where F=List and G=Id, the counit ε must be a natural transformation from List to Id (ε: List ⟹ Id). However, 'nat-concat' (flatten) is a transformation from List∘List to List (the monad multiplication μ). This definition will fail the triangle identity checks (specifically verify-triangle-right) because 'concat' will be applied to a list of atoms instead of a list of lists.
issues.code_snippet:
(define adj-free-list
  (make-adjunction
   'free-list
   functor-list
   functor-id
   nat-pure-list ; η : Id ⟹ List (singleton)
   nat-concat    ; ε : List∘List ⟹ List (flatten)
   ))
issues.suggested_fix: Correct the adjunction to use the proper forgetful functor for monoids as the right adjoint, or if a monad-derived adjunction is intended, ensure the categories and functors match the Monad-to-Adjunction construction (e.g., Kleisli or Eilenberg-Moore).

issues.description: adjunction-compose does not verify that its arguments are valid adjunctions. Since adjunction-left and others return #f for invalid inputs, calling functor-fmap on these results will cause a runtime crash.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a guard clause using (adjunction? adj1) and (adjunction? adj2) at the beginning of the function and return #f or signal an error if they are invalid.

issues.description: The galois? predicate only checks the symbol tag and not the length of the list, unlike adjunction?. This could lead to crashes in galois-lower or galois-upper if an undersized list is passed.
In adjunction-compose, the functor-fmap of the component functors is looked up every time the mapping function is called. These lookups can be hoisted out of the lambda for better performance.
issues.code_snippet:
(let ([new-left (make-functor (lambda (f x) ((functor-fmap F-prime) (lambda (y) ((functor-fmap F) f y)) x)))]
      [new-right (make-functor (lambda (f x) ((functor-fmap G) (lambda (y) ((functor-fmap G-prime) f y)) x)))])
issues.suggested_fix: Bind (functor-fmap F) and (functor-fmap F-prime) to variables in the outer let* and use those variables inside the lambda.

summary: The adjunction implementation has a significant correctness issue in the 'adj-free-list' example, which incorrectly uses monad multiplication as an adjunction counit for an identity right adjoint. There are also missing safety checks in 'adjunction-compose' and 'galois?' that could lead to crashes, and a minor performance optimization opportunity in functor composition.
